findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result object ({ success, data }) instead of the parsed data, so the wrapper is persisted as the credential key on every refresh in all modes, causing googleCredentialSchema parsing to fail on next load and breaking Google Calendar after the first token refresh

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — when credential sync is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response regardless of the wrapped refresh function's return shape, so Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin callers reading res?.data / accessToken / tokenInfo.data.error throw TypeError in sync mode; the () => any / implicit any return typing hides this at compile time

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 — passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId, so the sync endpoint is queried for the wrong user, and since credential ids are always truthy, sync is also attempted for team credentials with no user

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-9 — computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the schema only keeps access_token and zod strips all other fields (expiry, expires_in, instance_url, etc.); combined with the placeholder on line 25 the stored credential becomes { access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token" }, losing expiry tracking and overwriting real refresh tokens in the DB

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264 — parseRefreshTokenResponse injects refresh_token: "refresh_token" when the response lacks one, and that data is spread over o365AuthCredentials; Microsoft does not always return a new refresh token, so the real refresh token is clobbered by the placeholder and the next refresh fails

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:50 — appStoreMetadata is keyed by app directory name (googlecalendar, office365calendar, zoomvideo) but the lookup uses App.slug from the DB (google-calendar, office365-calendar, zoom), so any app whose slug differs from its dirName returns 404 "App not found", including the main calendar and video apps

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no shared secret or auth header (only calcomUserId and appSlug), so anyone who learns the endpoint URL can request live access tokens for arbitrary users; the response status is also never checked before the body is consumed

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27 — webhook secret is compared with !==, a non-constant-time comparison on a long-lived shared secret; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98 — getClient now performs a Salesforce refresh-token round trip plus prisma.credential.update on every call unconditionally, even when the access token is still valid (previously jsforce refreshed lazily via refreshFn), adding latency to every calendar operation and consuming Salesforce token-refresh quota; it also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens so Salesforce still hits the provider directly in sync mode

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — success is checked with response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok; statusText is an optional reason phrase (empty under HTTP/2 and some proxies), so valid 200 responses can be rejected with a 400 HttpError; hard-coding login.salesforce.com also breaks sandbox orgs that authenticated via test.salesforce.com

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-73 — findFirst by userId+appId then update/create is not atomic and assumes at most one credential per user per app; users can hold several credentials for the same app so the webhook silently overwrites an arbitrary one, concurrent calls can create duplicates, and the decrypted keys blob is stored without validation against the app's credential schema

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17,31,57 — no req.method check (GET writes credentials), and schema.parse and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw uncaught, producing 500s instead of 400s for malformed input or a wrong encryption key

packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — the slug sent to the sync endpoint is "zoomvideo" (the dirName) while every other adapter sends the DB slug; Zoom's slug is "zoom", so the sync endpoint receives an identifier that doesn't match what the webhook side expects

packages/lib/constants.ts:103 — APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the raw value of CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (string | undefined, not a boolean), so a flag-named constant actually holds the encryption key and invites accidental logging or serialization; should be wrapped in Boolean(...) / !!

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 and .env.example:237 — Node lowercases incoming header names but the code indexes req.headers with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim, guarded only by a comment; a mixed-case value makes every request 403 with no diagnostic; should lowercase in code

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-73 — findFirst by userId+appId then update/create is not atomic and assumes at most one credential per user per app; users can hold several credentials for the same app so the webhook silently overwrites an arbitrary one, concurrent calls can create duplicates, and the decrypted keys blob is stored without validation against the app's credential schema

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler does a read-then-write sequence: `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by `update` or `create`. This is not atomic; concurrent webhook calls can both see “no record” and both `create`, producing duplicates unless there is a DB-level unique constraint (not shown/handled here). Also, using `findFirst` (not `findUnique`) means if multiple credentials already exist for the same (userId, appId), the code will update an arbitrary matching record (ordering unspecified), effectively overwriting one credential without detecting ambiguity. Finally, the decrypted `keys` are only `JSON.parse`’d and written to `credential.key` with no schema/shape validation for the specific app, which is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 and .env.example:237 — Node lowercases incoming header names but the code indexes req.headers with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim, guarded only by a comment; a mixed-case value makes every request 403 with no diagnostic; should lowercase in code

adjudication.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` the secret check indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` verbatim:
```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]
```
In Node/Next.js, incoming header names are normalized to lowercase keys on `req.headers`. The `.env.example` only documents (via comment) that `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` "should be in lowercase", but the code does not enforce `.toLowerCase()`. If an operator sets a mixed-case value (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), the lookup will miss and the endpoint will always 403 even with a correct header present. This is a real correctness/config-robustness bug introduced by relying on a comment rather than normalizing in code.
